briefing.title: Wednesday, September 30
briefing.intro: Good morning! It's Wednesday, September 30. In Toronto it's 22 degrees right now, heading for a high of 23 with overcast skies. Here's your briefing: 3 stories from across Canada and 3 in AI and tech.

chapters.title: Good morning
chapters.text: Good morning! It's Wednesday, September 30. In Toronto it's 22 degrees right now, heading for a high of 23 with overcast skies. Here's your briefing: 3 stories from across Canada and 3 in AI and tech.

chapters.title: Canada
chapters.text: First, the top stories from across Canada.

chapters.title: Conservative MP Scott Aitchison Announces Fall Resignation
chapters.text: CBC News reports that Conservative MP Scott Aitchison will step down at the end of the fall sitting, ending a three‑decade public career that began as mayor of Huntsville. He cited a desire for a new chapter and reflected on his work on housing affordability as the party’s housing critic. Poilievre called him a dedicated public servant who never forgot his community.

chapters.title: Carney urges action on residential school reconciliation
chapters.text: CBC News · Top Stories reports Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada must move beyond remembrance and act on the Truth and Reconciliation Commission’s ninety‑four Calls to Action. He reminded listeners that more than 150,000 Indigenous children were forced into abusive residential schools and that the federal government bears responsibility for the lasting harm. The day’s ceremonies across the country honor survivors and call for honest dialogue and concrete steps forward.

chapters.title: Four people hit by vehicle on B.C.’s Tsawwassen First Nation in medical incident, police say
chapters.text: Four pedestrians were hit by a vehicle on the Tsawwassen First Nation in British Columbia during Wednesday’s National Day for Truth and Reconciliation event, police said. The collision occurred at roughly 11 a.m., and authorities described it as a medical incident, with emergency services treating the victims. CBC News · Top Stories reports the area is being asked to avoid the scene while the investigation continues.

chapters.title: AI & Tech
chapters.text: Now, the latest in AI and technology.

chapters.title: Meta and OpenAI Plan AI‑Powered Wearable Devices
chapters.text: The Verge reports that Meta and OpenAI are moving ahead with wearable AI devices despite earlier hardware setbacks. OpenAI’s design, partnered with Jony Ive, targets a launch no earlier than February 2027, while Meta’s Muse Charm pendant is slated for the upcoming holiday season. Both firms are betting that cute, useful AI agents will win over users.

chapters.title: ElevenLabs doubles valuation to $22 billion in employee tender
chapters.text: TechCrunch · AI reports ElevenLabs has opened a $300 million tender allowing staff to cash out at a $22 billion valuation, double the $11 billion level from its February funding round. The transaction, co-led by Wellington and T Rowe Price, follows a prior $100 million tender at a $6.6 billion valuation. This move reflects a growing trend of AI firms using secondary sales to retain talent.

chapters.title: Tech CEOs Sign Self‑Regulation Pledge on AI Safety
chapters.text: The Verge · AI reports that after a dinner with top tech leaders, President Trump announced a new AI safety plan. Six CEOs—from Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, XAI and Nvidia—signed a voluntary pledge to self‑regulate their AI systems. They said the accord is a meaningful start for industry‑wide responsibility, though it carries no binding legal force.

chapters.title: Sign-off
chapters.text: That's your briefing for this Wednesday. Have a wonderful day, and I'll talk to you tomorrow morning.

stories.headline: Conservative MP Scott Aitchison Announces Fall Resignation
stories.original_title: Conservative MP Scott Aitchison officially signals his intent to resign later this fall
stories.summary: Ontario Conservative MP Scott Aitchison said he will resign his Parry Sound‑Muskoka seat at the end of the fall sitting, after 30 years in public life. He thanked constituents, highlighted his work on housing affordability and noted his role as the party’s housing critic. Prime Minister Pierre Poilievre praised his service.

stories.headline: Carney urges action on residential school reconciliation
stories.original_title: ‘We owe them action,’ Carney says on Truth and Reconciliation Day
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada owes residential school survivors more than remembrance, calling for action on the Truth and Reconciliation Commission’s ninety‑four Calls to Action. He noted that over 150,000 Indigenous children were taken to abusive, under‑funded schools and that the federal government bears responsibility for the lasting harm.

stories.headline: Four people hit by vehicle on B.C.’s Tsawwassen First Nation in medical incident, police say
stories.original_title: Four people hit by vehicle on B.C.’s Tsawwassen First Nation in medical incident, police say
stories.summary: Four pedestrians were struck by a vehicle on the Tsawwassen First Nation in British Columbia during the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation event on Wednesday, police said. The collision occurred around 11 a.m. local time. Police described it as a medical incident and emergency services are treating the victims. The area is being avoided.

stories.headline: Meta and OpenAI Plan AI‑Powered Wearable Devices
stories.summary: Meta and OpenAI are preparing new wearable AI devices after previous hardware attempts struggled. OpenAI, working with designer Jony Ive, aims to ship a device no earlier than February 2027, while Meta plans to release its Muse Charm pendant before the holiday season. Both companies hope cute, useful agents will boost adoption.

stories.headline: ElevenLabs doubles valuation to $22 billion in employee tender
stories.original_title: AI voice startup ElevenLabs doubles valuation to $22B
stories.summary: ElevenLabs announced a $300 million tender that lets employees sell shares at a $22 billion valuation, twice the $11 billion level reached after its February $500 million raise. The deal was co-led by Wellington and T Rowe Price and follows a similar $100 million tender at a $6.6 billion valuation in September 2025.

stories.headline: Tech CEOs Sign Self‑Regulation Pledge on AI Safety
stories.original_title: Here’s what AI leaders are saying about Trump’s new safety plan
stories.summary: President Trump hosted leading AI executives who signed a Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities, a voluntary safety pledge. The signatories include Sundar Pichai, Dario Amodei, Mark Zuckerberg, Greg Brockman, Elon Musk and Jensen Huang. They described the accord as a positive step toward responsible AI development and job creation, while no legal enforcement mechanisms were included.
